claim: The four-state Select Opponent surface at $1C70 already collapses into a downstream gameplay-handoff split at L008B87: selector values 0..2 enable an opponent car by setting $1C76 = 1 and preserving the rival index in $1C7A, while selector value 3 disables opponent-side branches by setting $1C76 = 0 and forcing $1C7A back to 0 as a reused placeholder.

collapse_cases.notes: The three car cells keep opponent mode enabled and preserve the selected rival index.
The clock slot disables opponent-side branches and reuses rival index 0 as a placeholder instead of carrying a distinct fourth car index.

downstream_consumers.effect: Selects an 8-byte record from 01:8384..01:838A before the CGRAM upload at 0x00A0.
Selects a 0x20-byte block from 01:8614 + ($1C7A << 5) for VRAM 0x60C0.
Selects the bank-2 tables at 02:8306 / 02:830C that feed the 14DC and 13FC buffers.
Branches to L00948A when opponent mode is enabled and jumps to L009568 when it is disabled.
Gates the extra opponent-side initialization of 129B/1283/11E1/11F3/125F/1271.
Gates the second actor/path update through the y = 2 branch.
Gates later opponent-side runtime work before the path falls through toward L0127B8.

evidence: At L008B87, the code loads X = 1 and A = $1C70, then only on $1C70 == 3 executes dex and lda #$0000 before storing X -> $1C76 and A -> $1C7A.
For selector values 0..2, the same path stores $1C76 = 1 and preserves A = $1C70 into $1C7A.
The fourth Select Opponent slot is already visually closed as a helper-8 BG1 stopwatch/clock surface in tools/out/snes_frontend_select_opponent_clock_summary.json.
$1C7A is later consumed by rival-facing table loads in bank 1 and bank 2, while $1C76 gates opponent-side branches in both banks.
notes: This closes the immediate handoff distinction between the three rival-car cells and the fourth clock slot.

The exact timer or HUD behavior of the no-opponent branch is still not directly observed in a live gameplay capture, so the stronger reading is 'no-opponent split verified, full time-only semantics still probable'.
